Download an event log that amorem does not redistribute

Source: R/fetch_dataset.R
fetch_dataset.Rd

Seven of the data sets used in the package articles and in the amorem paper come from sources that state no licence for the data, so the package does not ship them. fetch_dataset() downloads the file from its original source, checks its MD5 sum, builds the same tidy table that earlier versions bundled, caches it and returns it.

Usage

fetch_dataset(
  name,
  cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("amorem", "cache"),
  refresh = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

name

One of "classroom_events", "classroom_actors", "social_evolution_calls", "social_evolution_actors", "social_evolution_friendship", "college_msg", "email_eu_core".

cache_dir

Folder for the downloaded file and the built table. The default, tools::R_user_dir("amorem", "cache"), keeps them between sessions; pass tempdir() to keep nothing.

refresh

If TRUE, download and build again even when a cached copy exists.

quiet

If TRUE, download without progress messages.

Value

A data frame, the same object as the data set of that name in amorem 1.2.0.

Data sets

classroom_events, classroom_actors

691 directed interactions among 20 people in one US high-school class period on 16 October 1996 (McFarland 2001), and the actors' sex and role. Columns of the events: time (minutes since the start of the period), sender, receiver, interaction_type (factor: social, sanction, task) and weight (1 for communication directed at particular others, 501 rows; 0.2 for broadcast communication such as lecturing, 190 rows). Rows are in time order, ties by sender and then receiver. Columns of the actors: id, sex (F, M), role (instructor, grade_11, grade_12). Source: McFarland, D. (2001). Student resistance: How the formal and informal organization of classrooms facilitate everyday forms of student defiance. American Journal of Sociology 107(3), 612–678, doi:10.1086/338779 ; downloaded from the networkDynamic repository (https://github.com/statnet/networkDynamic, object McFarland_cls33_10_16_96). No licence is stated for the data.

social_evolution_calls, social_evolution_actors, social_evolution_friendship

439 phone calls among 84 undergraduates of an MIT residence hall, 6 September to 18 October 2008, with the actors' attributes (id, present, floor, gradeType) and 766 friendship survey events (replace is 1 when a tie is added, 0 when it is removed). time is in days since the first call; attr(., "unix_origin") holds the Unix time of time = 0. Source: Madan, A., Cebrian, M., Moturu, S., Farrahi, K., Pentland, A. (2012). Sensing the "health state" of a community. IEEE Pervasive Computing 11(4), 36–45, doi:10.1109/MPRV.2011.79 ; downloaded from the goldfish repository (https://github.com/stocnet/goldfish, object Social_Evolution). No licence is stated for the data, and the original MIT Reality Commons release asks users not to redistribute them and not to attempt to re-identify participants.

college_msg

59,835 private messages between students of the University of California, Irvine over 193 days in 2004. time is in days since the first message; attr(., "unix_origin") holds its date-time. Source: Panzarasa, P., Opsahl, T., Carley, K. (2009). Patterns and dynamics of users' behavior and interaction: Network analysis of an online community. Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology 60(5), 911–932; downloaded from SNAP, https://snap.stanford.edu/data/CollegeMsg.html. No licence is stated; SNAP asks users to cite the source.

email_eu_core

12,216 e-mails between the members of one department of a European research institution over 803 days, self-addressed e-mails removed. time is in days. Source: Paranjape, A., Benson, A. R., Leskovec, J. (2017). Motifs in temporal networks. WSDM '17, 601–610, doi:10.1145/3018661.3018731 ; downloaded from SNAP, file email-Eu-core-temporal-Dept3.txt.gz of https://snap.stanford.edu/data/email-Eu-core-temporal.html. No licence is stated; SNAP asks users to cite the source.

Examples

# \donttest{
# needs an internet connection the first time
ev <- tryCatch(fetch_dataset("classroom_events", cache_dir = tempdir()),
               error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(ev)) head(ev)
#>    time sender receiver interaction_type weight
#> 1 0.125     14       12           social      1
#> 2 0.250     12       14           social      1
#> 3 0.375     18       12         sanction      1
#> 4 0.500     12       18         sanction      1
#> 5 0.625      1       12         sanction      1
#> 6 0.750     12        1         sanction      1
# }
